title: T2WI-based intratumoral habitat and peritumoral radiomics to predict lymph node metastasis in cervical cancer: a multicenter study with biological validation
abstract: Abstract Background To develop and validate a T2WI-based nomogram integrating intratumoral habitat imaging, peritumoral radiomics, and clinical features for preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis (LNM) in cervical cancer (CC), and to verify the biological plausibility of imaging habitats using an animal model. Methods This multicenter study included 766 CC patients (IB1-IIA2 and IIIC) from four centers, divided into training (n = 219), internal validation (n = 94), and two external test cohorts (n = 269, n = 184) between 2020 and 2024. Habitat imaging and peritumoral features were extracted, followed by machine‑learning model construction, evaluation, and SHAP interpretability. For biological validation, 12 nude mice bearing HeLa, SiHa, and U14 tumors underwent 9.4T MRI; imaging-pathology spatial registration was performed using 3D-printed molds, and habitat consistency was quantified by the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) and intraclass correlation coefficient for area (ICC(area)). Results Clinical stage and tumor diameter ≥ 4 cm were independent risk factors for LNM (both P < 0.05). The combined model yielded AUCs of 0.933 (training), 0.898 (internal validation), and 0.858–0.863 (external tests). A nomogram with a Youden-derived cutoff of 0.32 demonstrated consistent sensitivity (0.818–0.913) and specificity (0.732–0.877) across cohorts, with good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.183–0.561). Animal experiments revealed moderate spatial correspondence (ARI: 0.4–0.6) and high proportional consistency (ICC (area): 0.8–1.0) between imaging and pathological habitats. Conclusions This T2WI-based intratumoral habitat and peritumoral radiomics model provides accurate, economical preoperative LNM prediction for CC to guide personalized radiotherapy or surgery, with biological validity confirmed by animal experiments. title: Core Decompression via the Flip Cutter Technique Using an Expandable Reamer Augmented with Platelet-Rich Plasma and Calcium Phosphate Cement for Early-Stage (ARCO 1–2) Avascular Necrosis of the Femoral Head: A Single Centre Retrospective Observational Study
abstract: Abstract Background Avascular necrosis of the femoral head (AVNFH) frequently progresses to subchondral collapse and requires total hip arthroplasty if untreated. Core decompression (CD) provides a joint preserving intervention for early-stage disease. This study evaluates the short-term clinical and radiological outcomes of CD using the flip cutter technique of expandable reamer (ER), augmented with platelet-rich plasma (PRP) and calcium phosphate cement (CPC). Methods This uncontrolled retrospective single-centre observational study evaluated 25 hips in patients with symptomatic ARCO stage 1–2 AVNFH treated between January 2023 and January 2025. The surgical technique involved sequential debridement of necrotic bone through a minimal cortical window using ER, followed by PRP injection and sealing of the cortical defect with CPC. Patients were encouraged to bear weight immediately as tolerated. Outcomes were assessed in 6 weeks, and 3, 6, and 12 months using Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain scores, Harris Hip Scores (HHS), hip range of motion (ROM), and serial imaging, including a 1-year follow-up MRI. Results At the 12-month follow-up, the combined intervention was associated with a significant improvement in mean VAS pain scores, HHS and hip ROM (p < 0.05). Radiographic and MRI assessments confirmed no disease progression or subchondral collapse in any hip at one-year. The day-case procedure was performed safely with no recorded complications. Conclusion In this small retrospective study, ER-assisted core decompression with PRP and CPC was associated with improved short-term pain and functional scores, with no observed subchondral collapse or conversion to THA during approximately one year of follow-up. These findings should be interpreted as preliminary observations rather than evidence of definitive efficacy, and they require confirmation in adequately powered prospective comparative studies with longer-term follow-up. Novelty Statement By evaluating a tri-modal, minimally invasive technique combining expandable reamer debridement, platelet-rich plasma augmentation, and a calcium phosphate cement seal, this study provides preliminary evidence that this combined approach can potentially arrest disease progression and prevent subchondral collapse at one-year follow-up. Trial Registration: Not applicable, as this evaluation is based on retrospective clinical data and does not constitute a prospective healthcare trial. Level of Evidence: IV (Retrospective)

title: Multimodal MR Radiomics for Preoperative Prediction of Perineural Invasion and Prognostic Stratification in Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma
abstract: Abstract Background To develop and validate a multimodal model integrating multiphasic contrast-enhanced MRI radiomics with clinical-imaging information for the preoperative prediction of perineural invasion (PNI) in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) and for postoperative risk stratification. Methods Patients with ICC treated at the Eastern Hepatobiliary Surgery Hospital between September 2014 and February 2025 were retrospectively enrolled ( n = 455) and randomly assigned to training ( n = 232), testing ( n = 99) and validation ( n = 124) cohorts. Radiomic features were extracted with PyRadiomics from tumor regions on all four phases and selected by LASSO regression; the clinical-imaging, radiomics and multimodal models were built with logistic regression. Discrimination, calibration and clinical net benefit were assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA). Overall survival (OS) and recurrence-free survival (RFS) were compared by the Kaplan-Meier

title: A retrospective study for prediction severity of hypertriglyceridemia-associated acute pancreatitis patients and association with in-hospital mortality
abstract: Abstract Background : Hypertriglyceridemia-associated acute pancreatitis (HTG-AP) is the second leading cause of acute pancreatitis (AP) in China. This study aimed to identify HTG-AP severity and clarify the association between the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and in-hospital mortality in severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) patients. Method: A total of 289 HTG-AP patients were separated into SAP (n=104) and non-SAP (n=185) groups in Xuanwu Hospital from 2014 to 2023. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to developed a formula based on laboratory tests and clinical assessments for predicting the severity of AP. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) was used to elucidate the link between the TyG index and in-hospital mortality. Results: Both SAP and non-SAP patients had a median onset age of 39 years (68.2% male). SAP patients presented higher serum levels of D-Dimer, triglycerides, glucose, blood urea nitrogen, creatinine, procalcitonin, C-reactive protein, and interleukin-6, along with lower levels of calcium and ALB, accompanied by significant values of the TyG index and scores of the acute physiology and chronic health evaluation (APACHE-II) and modified computed tomography severity index (p<0.05). The multivariable logistic regression demonstrated superior predictive performance, with an AUC of 0.940, a specificity of 0.784, and a sensitivity of 0.990. A non-linear relationship was observed between the TyG index within 24 hours of admission and in-hospital mortality across Days 7, 30, and 120. Conclusion : This study developed a multivariable logistic regression model incorporating the TyG index, APACHE II score, and serum creatinine to predict SAP and highlight the prognostic value of the TyG index in HTG-AP.

title: Borderline Breast Phyllodes Tumor Coexisting with Intermediate- Grade Ductal Carcinoma In Situ and Focal Invasion: A Case Report and Literature Review
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Borderline phyllodes tumor (PT) coexisting with ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) and invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) is an exceptionally rare mixed breast lesion. Due to its low incidence and compositional complexity, it poses substantial diagnostic and management challenges. We present such a case to highlight the pitfalls in preoperative diagnosis and the rationale for a multidisciplinary therapeutic strategy. Presentation of case: A 72-year-old Chinese female presented with a 2-week history of a right breast mass. Ultrasound and mammography revealed a large (52.6 mm), well-circumscribed, lobulated solid mass (BI-RADS 4A/4B), suggestive of a phyllodes tumor. Core needle biopsy returned “fibroadenoma with usual ductal hyperplasia.” Subsequent lumpectomy showed borderline PT (80%), intermediate-grade DCIS (20%), and focal Grade II invasive carcinoma of no special type (< 1%, maximal invasive diameter 3 mm). Immunohistochemistry of the invasive component: ER(−), PR(−), HER-2(3+), Ki-67 60%. Given the patient’s preference against breast conservation, a right total mastectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy was performed (0/1 nodes positive). Final staging: pT1aN0M0, Stage IA, HER-2 overexpression subtype. No adjuvant chemotherapy, targeted therapy, or radiotherapy was given. At 12-month follow-up, no local or distant recurrence was observed. Conclusion Definitive diagnosis of PT coexisting with DCIS and IDC relies on adequate excision specimens rather than biopsy alone. Clinical management should integrate PT behavior with standard breast cancer guidelines through multidisciplinary collaboration, balancing complete oncologic control against the risk of overtreatment. Longer follow-up is warranted to confirm durable outcomes.

title: A multimodal fusion model combining transfer-learning ultrasound deep features and clinical risk factors for predicting cervical lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma: a multicentre retrospective study
abstract: Abstract Background Cervical lymph node metastasis (CLNM) is the most common route of spread in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) and a key determinant of surgical extent, radioactive iodine therapy and recurrence risk. Pre-operative ultrasound has limited sensitivity for nodal disease, and objective, reproducible risk-stratification tools are needed. We developed and validated a multimodal model fusing deep ultrasound image features with clinical risk factors, compared it with clinical and image-only models, and evaluated its transportability in an independent external cohort. Methods In this multicentre retrospective study, 607 consecutive PTC patients (2022–2026; N1, 48.4%) with pre-operative grey-scale ultrasound and definitive histopathology were included, plus an external validation set of 252 consecutive patients (N1, 83.3%). Lesions were segmented by a YOLOv8-seg model trained on 390 manually labelled frames (mask mAP50 = 0.985), retaining 1,322 network-generated masks and making delineation operator-independent. The development cohort was split 7:3 into training (n = 424) and internal validation (n = 183) sets; univariable and multivariable logistic regression identified independent clinical risk factors. Ultrasound deep features (896-d pooled activations) were extracted by a same-domain transfer-pretrained backbone, reduced to 30 principal components and fused with clinical factors in a logistic regression head. Models were evaluated by AUC with bootstrap 95% CIs, DeLong tests, calibration curves, DCA and SHAP. Results Age (OR 0.959, 95% CI 0.936–0.982), female sex (OR 0.316, 0.178–0.564), tumour diameter (OR 5.321, 2.438–11.617), minimal extrathyroidal extension (OR 2.001, 1.071–3.741) and multifocality (OR 6.106, 2.178–17.118) were independent predictors. On internal validation, the clinical, ultrasound deep-learning and fusion models achieved AUCs of 0.709 (0.641–0.777), 0.642 (0.561–0.723) and 0.737 (0.665–0.808); the fusion model significantly outperformed the imaging model (dAUC = 0.094, P = 0.0015) and showed the highest net benefit on DCA. The clinical model showed limited transportability in the external validation set (n = 252; AUC = 0.528), consistent with case-mix-dependent shift. Conclusions Fusing same-domain transfer-learning ultrasound deep features with clinical risk factors achieved the highest internal-validation AUC and clinical net benefit, significantly outperforming image-only modelling; external validation of the fusion model remains to be performed. The same-domain transfer strategy offers a reproducible paradigm for small-sample medical imaging tasks.

title: Posterior cortical gray matter heterogeneity between hyposmia- and RBD-defined prodromal phenotypes in Parkinson's disease: a PPMI voxel-based morphometry study
abstract: Abstract Background Prodromal Parkinson's disease (PD) includes clinically distinct enrollment phenotypes. We examined whole-brain gray matter volume (GMV) in Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) participants recruited through hyposmia-only or REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD)-only pathways and assessed the stability of the findings. Methods Baseline T1-weighted MRI from 465 hyposmia-only and 149 RBD-only participants (N = 614) was analyzed with CAT12/SPM25 voxel-based morphometry (VBM). Models included age, sex, intracranial volume, and scanner family. Whole-brain clusters were defined at voxel p < 0.001 and tested using family-wise error (FWE) correction. We examined scanner-restricted samples, 123 sex/scanner-matched pairs, and 10,000-sign-flip permutation analysis of linear models (PALM). Bilateral cuneus/calcarine estimates and clinical assessments were exploratory. Results Whole-brain analysis identified a posterior phenotype effect (F cluster: k = 4,499; pFWE = 4.15×10⁻⁷), with higher GMV in hyposmia-only participants. In 123 matched pairs, a posterior H > RBD T cluster survived correction (pFWE = 0.0266), whereas the F contrast did not. PALM also identified a posterior effect (two-sided threshold-free cluster enhancement [TFCE] FWE p = 0.0027; voxelwise FWE p = 0.0277). Adjusted bilateral cuneus differences were + 0.211 mL (95% CI 0.095–0.327) in the full cohort and + 0.187 mL (0.041–0.333) after matching. MRI-proximal RBD screening questionnaire scores showed no significant association with regional GMV. Conclusions Posterior cortical GMV differed between these enrollment-defined prodromal phenotypes. The anatomical finding was supported by nonparametric inference, although the matched F test and strictest scanner restriction were nonsignificant. Longitudinal studies are needed to establish its clinical relevance.

title: Bilateral Gluteal Pyomyositis Caused by Citrobacter Species: A Case Report from Sudan
abstract: Abstract Background: Pyomyositis is a bacterial infection of skeletal muscle that most commonly affects tropical populations and is usually caused by Staphylococcus aureus . Gram-negative organisms are uncommon causes, and Citrobacter species are rarely reported. Case presentation: A 27-year-old Sudanese man with no known chronic medical illness presented with an 8-day history of high-grade fever followed by severe bilateral hip pain and gluteal swelling. Initial investigations showed leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and a positive typhoid IgM test, and ceftriaxone was initiated. During hospitalization, he developed progressive bilateral gluteal swelling, severe pain, and restricted hip movement. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated bilateral gluteal and peri-hip muscle inflammation with large intramuscular fluid collections consistent with pyomyositis. Image-guided aspiration yielded purulent material, from which Citrobacter species was isolated. Surgical drainage was recommended but declined by the patient. He was subsequently treated with repeated image-guided aspiration and two weeks of intravenous ciprofloxacin according to susceptibility testing, with marked clinical improvement and restoration of full hip movement. At three-week follow-up, he remained asymptomatic without clinical evidence of recurrence. Conclusion: Bilateral gram-negative pyomyositis caused by Citrobacter species is an unusual presentation in a previously healthy young adult. MRI and microbiological examination of aspirated material were important for diagnosis and targeted therapy. This case also illustrates that repeated percutaneous aspiration combined with appropriate antimicrobial therapy may provide an alternative source-control strategy when operative drainage is declined, although surgical or percutaneous drainage remains the recommended approach for established intramuscular abscesses.

This case also illustrates that repeated percutaneous aspiration combined with appropriate antimicrobial therapy may provide an alternative source-control strategy when operative drainage is declined, although surgical or percutaneous drainage remains the recommended approach for established intramuscular abscesses.

title: A foundation model for three-dimensional anatomical reconstruction from sparse X-ray projections
abstract: Abstract Computed tomography (CT) provides three-dimensional anatomical information but requires costly scanners and exposes patients to higher radiation doses than conventional X-ray imaging. Reconstructing three-dimensional anatomy from a few X-ray projections could extend widely available X-ray systems beyond two-dimensional imaging. We present SPARC, a foundation model pretrained once on 47,149 chest scans across diverse acquisition settings, enabling a single model to be adapted to different X-ray imaging configurations and anatomical regions. Across eight datasets covering five body regions, seven mainly outside the chest, SPARC reconstructed volumes with greater fidelity than five existing methods, exceeding the strongest in peak signal-to-noise ratio by 0.8-2.6 dB with eight projections and 1.4-2.7 dB with four. CT-based tools for abnormality classification and organ segmentation retained most of their performance when applied directly to SPARC's reconstructions from eight projections, fewer than 3% of the hundreds recorded by a CT scanner. They reached 98% of their area under the receiver operating characteristic curve on CT for 18 chest abnormalities, and 86% and 93% of their Dice score on CT for abdominal organs and lung lobes, with Dice scores 8.8% and 4.4% higher, in relative terms, than with the best competing method. Pretraining considerably increased the adaptation data efficiency. With ten patients, SPARC reconstructed chest CT more accurately than the same architecture trained from scratch on 100 patients. With the models and code released, SPARC could support the clinical translation of sparse-view reconstruction and expand access to three-dimensional imaging where CT scanners are unavailable.

title: Feasibility of chronic kidney disease classification using bilateral kidney ultrasound and foundation model representations
abstract: Abstract Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major global health burden, yet early diagnosis remains challenging and conventional kidney ultrasonography is limited by operator dependence and low sensitivity to subtle textural changes. We investigated the feasibility of an ultrasound foundation model for CKD classification from bilateral kidney ultrasound images, with reference labels defined using an operational subset of the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) 2024 guidelines. In this retrospective single-center study, 13,245 kidney ultrasound images from 1,484 patients (1,128 with CKD and 356 without) were analyzed. The Universal Ultrasound Foundation Model (USFM) was compared with five fine-tuned deep learning architectures (VGG16, ResNet-50, DenseNet-121, EfficientNet-B0, and Vision Transformer) over 10 random seeds, with performance assessed at the sample and examination levels. USFM achieved the highest mean values for most metrics, although its confidence intervals overlapped with those of the strongest baseline, and it showed greater stability across repeated experiments. At the examination level, it achieved a balanced accuracy of 74.49 ± 4.63\%, an F1-score of 73.59 ± 3.60\%, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 84.80 ± 1.98\%, with comparable results at the sample level. These findings support the feasibility of ultrasound foundation models for CKD classification from bilateral kidney ultrasound images and motivate external validation.

title: Dual-Wield: An Observational Study of Utilization and Outcomes of Cryobiopsy and Intraoperative CT scan During Navigational Bronchoscopy
abstract: Abstract Background Pulmonary nodules are common incidental imaging findings, and distinguishing malignant from benign etiologies frequently requires invasive sampling. CT-guided transthoracic needle biopsy offers high yield but carries pneumothorax rates of 15–45% and precludes concurrent mediastinal staging. Shape-sensing navigational bronchoscopy, intraprocedural cone-beam CT (CBCT), and transbronchial cryobiopsy have each independently improved bronchoscopy performance, but integration of all three into one workflow remains poorly characterized. We describe real-world utilization and outcomes of these modalities at a large volume community tertiary care center. Research Question What is the real-world utilization, diagnostic performance, and complication rate of navigational bronchoscopy for lung nodule sampling with the addition of CBCT and cryobiopsy? Study Design and Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of navigational bronchoscopy procedures performed at a single community tertiary care center between January 1, 2024, and January 1, 2026. Two physician investigators independently abstracted procedure reports, imaging, and pathology from the electronic health record, recording cryobiopsy use, CBCT use, target nodule size, pathology, and complications. Diagnostic yield was determined using the strict ATS/ACCP consensus definition. Results Among 199 navigational bronchoscopy procedures, 229 lesions were sampled. Mean nodule size was 22.4 ± 17.7 mm overall, smallest with cryobiopsy plus CBCT (17.4 ± 13.7 mm) and largest with no adjunctive modality (29.8 ± 20.3 mm). Overall diagnostic yield was 78.0%: 83.9% with cryobiopsy plus CBCT, 75.0% cryobiopsy alone, 70.4% CBCT alone, and 73.2% no adjunctive modality. The complication rate was 3.5% (7/199). Diagnostic yield trended higher in cases with both cryobiopsy and CBCT. Conclusion Integrating navigational bronchoscopy with CBCT and cryobiopsy achieved the highest diagnostic yield while sampling the smallest nodules with an acceptable safety profile. Prospective randomized studies are warranted to define the independent contribution of each adjunct and to detect any true incremental harm.

title: Artificial Intelligence–Driven Volumetric Quantification of Urinary Stone Burden and Hydronephrosis From CT Images
abstract: Abstract Purpose Given the limitations of conventional stone burden assessment based on maximum diameter or ellipsoid-derived volume estimates, we aimed to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)–based method for automated quantification of stone and hydronephrosis volumes from CT images. Materials and Methods A 2-step algorithm was developed. First, a U-Net incorporating residual blocks, dense blocks, a morphology-aware block, and attention gates (RDAM U-Net) segmented the kidneys; hyperparameters were optimized using Complex System Response (CSR) experimental design with 5-fold cross-validation. Second, within the segmented kidney, hydronephrosis was identified from low–Hounsfield unit (HU) regions, and renal stones from high-HU regions using morphological processing and 3-dimensional (3D) connected-component analysis. AI-derived stone volumes were compared with ellipsoid-based estimates using Pearson and Spearman correlation, Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC), intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), and Bland–Altman analysis. Results Eighty-two kidney CT cases were used for model development. RDAM U-Net achieved a mean intersection over union of 0.9432 and Dice coefficient of 0.9681, with fewer parameters and a 32.58% shorter parameter-update time than reference attention-based U-Nets. In 39 paired stone measurements, AI-derived and ellipsoid-estimated volumes showed a near-perfect correlation (Pearson r = 0.977; Spearman ρ = 0.966; R² = 0.954; all p < 0.001) and high agreement (Lin's CCC = 0.959; ICC = 0.960). AI volumes were systematically lower than ellipsoid estimates (mean difference, − 51.21 mm³; p = 0.001), with the difference increasing with stone volume. HU-based composition analysis agreed with the clinical record in 12 of 13 classifiable stones (92.3%). Conclusions AI-based CT segmentation enabled automated volumetric quantification of both urinary stone burden and hydronephrosis, providing direct 3D assessment without reliance on geometric assumptions. Integrating stone volume, hydronephrosis volume, and stone composition into a single automated workflow may support more individualized surgical and metabolic management of urolithiasis. Further validation in larger external cohorts is warranted.

title: Analysis of Computed Tomography Image Features of Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma on The Basis of Machine Learning: Differentiation of High-Grade from Low-Grade Fuhrman Nuclear Grades
abstract: Abstract Background Previous researches have clarified potential clinical applications of radiomics-based prediction of tumor phenotype. The purpose of our research is to utilize radiomic features in computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) system of prediction for high Fuhrman nuclear grade and low Fuhrman nuclear grade in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (RCC) Methods We selected 110 images from 109 case number of axial contrast- enhanced computed tomography with a pathological diagnosis of clear cell RCC from The Cancer Imaging Achieve (TCIA) portal. After preprocessing and extraction of features of from radiological images, the Weka Experiment Environment was run to compare performance of different classifiers to predict high Fuhrman nuclear grade and low Fuhrman nuclear grade. Results Seventy features and 23 selected features were input into classifiers to predict high Fuhrman nuclear grade and low Fuhrman nuclear grade, respectively. The SVM based on poly-kernel classifier (Accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, area under the receiver operative characteristic curve (AUROC), precision, recall and F1 score were 82%, 82%, 82%, 82%, 82%, 82% and 82%, respectively) and K-Nearest neighbors (Accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, AUROC, precision, recall and F1 score were 90.91%, 91%, 89%, 90%, 92%, 91% and 91.5%. Respectively) showed significant better performance than other classifiers, such as Bagging (Bagging), Naive Bayes (NaiveBayes), Boosting (AdaBoostM1), Decision trees (J48), Bayesian Network (BayesNet), library Support vector machines (LibSVM), Artificial Neural Networks (Multilayer Perceptron), Logistic regression (Logistic), Random Forest Tree (RandomForest),respectively. Conclusions The developed CAD system generated by the optimal machine-learning methods with radiomic features is a non-invasive method of predicting and monitoring tumor-nuclear grading characteristics in image-defined response evaluation in clinical practice of targeted therapy of clear cell RCC. title: Predictive value of a nomogram model based on ultrasound and clinical features for axillary lymph node metastasis in patients with breast cancer: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Breast cancer (BC) is the most common malignancy in women, and axillary lymph node metastasis (ALNM) is closely associated with poorer prognosis and governs treatment decision-making. Current assessment relies mainly on sentinel lymph node biopsy, which is invasive and delays preoperative planning. This study aims to explore the predictive value of a nomogram model based on ultrasound and clinical features for ALNM in patients with breast cancer (BC). The clinical data of 193 BC patients treated in two hospitals from January 2022 to December 2024 were enrolled and retrospectively analyzed, of which, the clinical data of 113 patients from Nantong Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine were randomly divided into the training and internal validation cohorts at a 7:3 ratio, a predictive nomogram model for ALNM was constructed in the training cohort using a logistic regression to identify independent risk factors, and its performance was subsequently evaluated. Internal and external validations were carried out using the clinical data respectively from the internal validation cohort and the external validation cohort (80 patients) collected from Nantong Third People’s Hospital. CA125, elasticity modulus ratio, unclear boundaries, irregular edges, and blood flow resistance index were identified as risk factors for ALNM. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, calibration curve analysis, and decision curve analysis (DCA) demonstrated that the nomogram model established on these factors exhibited good discrimination, calibration, and clinical validity for predicting ALNM. Consistent results were also obtained in internal and external validation cohorts. The nomogram model based on ultrasound and clinical features demonstrates a promising predictive value for ALNM in BC patients, this study may provide a new auxiliary method for preoperative diagnosis of ALNM in BC patients. However, larger-scale multicenter validations are necessary to improve the generalizability of our model.

title: trans-Resveratrol and ε-viniferin recovery from grapevine pruning residues: process optimization and varietal screening towards industrial valorisation
abstract: Abstract Vine shoots are abundant viticultural by-products and promising renewable sources of high value stilbenoids for sustainable biorefinery applications. Stilbenoids are phytoalexins bearing phenolic moieties produced by Vitaceae under biotic and abiotic stress, and endowed with nutraceutical, cosmeceutical, and agrochemical potential. This study optimized the recovery of trans -resveratrol and ε-viniferin from vine shoots using Box–Behnken response surface methodology by evaluating extraction time (t), solvent mixture (S), and matrix-to-solvent ratio (R) as initial step of the circular economy task of European LIFE - Natural Agro project. The optimized conditions were then applied to conventional solid–liquid extraction (SLE), ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE), and Soxhlet extraction. The optimal conditions were 100% ethanol, R = 0.12 g mL⁻¹, and t = 35 min. Although Soxhlet extraction gave the highest extraction yield (EY%), UAE produced the most stilbene-enriched extract, with 9.50 mg g⁻¹ dry extract of trans -resveratrol and 25.66 mg g⁻¹ dry extract of ε-viniferin, while reducing extraction time and prolonged thermal exposure. The optimized UAE protocol was subsequently applied to grapevine varieties from Italy, Portugal, and France, revealing marked genotype-dependent differences in stilbene composition. ε-Viniferin was generally more abundant than trans -resveratrol, and Pinot Meunier, Grechetto Gentile, Moscato, and Moscatel Graudo were identified as promising raw materials, depending on the target compound. Spectrophotometric assays further confirmed variety-dependent differences in antioxidant activity, total phenolic content, and total flavonoid content. Overall, the proposed UAE strategy offers a simple, food-grade, and scalable approach for valorising vine-pruning residues as sources of bioactive ingredients.

title: Lung Cancer Classification from CT Images: A Comparative Study of SVM, Modified CNN, and EfficientNet–SVM Hybrid Models
abstract: Abstract This paper proposes a computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) framework that combines four complementary classification paradigms on the publicly available IQ-OTH/NCCD CT dataset with 1,097 slices across benign, malignant, and normal classes from 110 patients. The framework comprises: (i) an image-processing pipeline employing Gaussian smoothing, histogram equalization, Canny edge detection, and morphological closing, (ii) Otsu-based lung segmentation followed by handcrafted feature extraction combining statistical Local Binary Pattern (LBP), gradient, and shape descriptors, (iii) a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier benchmarked under a systematic ablation of three kernels and six class-balancing strategies (SMOTE, ADASYN, Borderline-SMOTE, Random Over-Sampling, SMOTE–Tomek, and cost-sensitive class weighting), (iv) a baseline convolutional neural network (CNN) and a modified CNN architecture enriched with batch normalization, and (v) a hybrid EfficientNet–SVM model that separates deep representation learning from maximum-margin decision-boundary fitting. The modified CNN achieves the highest overall test accuracy of 99.41% with a macro F1-score of 0.99, while the SVM with the RBF kernel under Random Over-Sampling reaches 98.81% balanced accuracy and the hybrid CNN–SVM attains 98.00% test accuracy. The result demonstrates both robust-ness across classes and competitiveness against recent state-of-the-art models on the same dataset.

title: Bone Density Architecture and Functional Cortical Thickness of the Greater Tuberosity: A CT-Based Analysis of 739 Proximal Humeri
abstract: Abstract Background The greater tuberosity (GT) is central to rotator cuff repair and proximal humerus fracture fixation, yet population-level data on its bone density architecture are lacking. This study characterizes the GT density profile, functional cortical thickness (FCT), and regional concordance with the calcar across age and sex subgroups. Methods In this retrospective cross-sectional study, computed tomography (CT)-derived Hounsfield unit (HU) values were analyzed in 739 left proximal humeri from a large CT-based bone morphometry database. A 5 mm cylindrical region of interest spanning the GT from posterior to anterior cortex (specimen-specific length, 25.5 ± 3.2 mm) sampled density at 21 points (5% relative-depth increments). Functional cortical thickness (FCT-200) was the number of consecutive increments from the posterior surface at or above 200 HU. Analyses comprised linear and logistic regression, ANCOVA and paired t-tests. Results The GT exhibited a U-shaped density profile: 320.9 HU at the posterior surface, a minimum of 7.1 HU at 45% relative depth, and 200.3 HU at the anterior cortex. Age explained 23.1% of variance (− 12.7 HU per decade; p < 0.001); sex explained an additional 4.9%. The cortical shell showed the largest absolute decline (− 22.7 HU per decade). In women older than 65 years, FCT-200 did not exceed one increment (≈ 1.15 mm) in 69.2%; in women, the probability of this finding exceeded 50% by age 56 (bootstrap 95% confidence interval [CI]: 50–61). Mean GT density was lower than calcar density in all age and sex subgroups (Δ = −48.5 HU; paired d = − 0.80; r = 0.716), so a 100 HU threshold classified 63.1% of specimens as low density at the GT but 40.7% at the calcar. Conclusions The GT has a U-shaped density architecture with a thin functional cortical shell that shows the largest absolute age-related decline; reduced functional cortical thickness in women is already common from the sixth decade. Because the GT is, on average, the lower-density site in all age and sex subgroups, calcar-derived density thresholds should not be assumed to be transferable to the GT. These data provide reference values that may inform anchor fixation and fracture management.

In women older than 65 years, FCT-200 did not exceed one increment (≈ 1.15 mm) in 69.2%; in women, the probability of this finding exceeded 50% by age 56 (bootstrap 95% confidence interval [CI]: 50–61). Mean GT density was lower than calcar density in all age and sex subgroups (Δ = −48.5 HU; paired d = − 0.80; r = 0.716), so a 100 HU threshold classified 63.1% of specimens as low density at the GT but 40.7% at the calcar. Conclusions The GT has a U-shaped density architecture with a thin functional cortical shell that shows the largest absolute age-related decline; reduced functional cortical thickness in women is already common from the sixth decade. Because the GT is, on average, the lower-density site in all age and sex subgroups, calcar-derived density thresholds should not be assumed to be transferable to the GT. These data provide reference values that may inform anchor fixation and fracture management.

title: Denoised gray matter BOLD-CSF coupling in aging and its association with markers of preclinical AD
abstract: Abstract Global gray matter (gGM) blood-oxygen-level-dependent (BOLD) signal fluctuations are temporally coupled with cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) inflow. Reduced gGM BOLD-CSF coupling has been reported in aging and linked to Alzheimer’s disease (AD)-related pathology. Our study aimed to investigate the effect of multi-echo denoising on age-related reductions in coupling and whether coupling is associated with cortical thickness across AD-vulnerable regions and crystallized–fluid ability (‘CF’) discrepancy, markers of preclinical AD. We analyzed an open-access behavioral/MRI dataset (n = 301) cognitively healthy younger and older adults (OpenNeuro ds003592). Coupling scores were calculated as correlations between gGM signal fluctuations and CSF inflow signals, before and after denoising. Linear mixed models tested the effects of age and denoising on coupling, while multiple regression models assessed associations between denoised coupling, cortical thickness, and CFdiscrepancy. Coupling was lower in older versus younger adults. Denoising significantly reduced coupling in younger adults but not in older adults. Both gGM and CSF signal amplitudes were lower in older adults. Denoised coupling was not significantly associated with cortical thickness or CFdiscrepancy, and cortical thickness was not associated with CFdiscrepancy after controlling for age. These findings support age-related differences in BOLD–CSF coupling, which itself may not be related to coarse markers of preclinical AD.

title: Birth-cohort effects and the limits of ecological evaluation of mammography screening: an age-period-cohort analysis of breast cancer mortality in Japan, 1958–2024
abstract: Abstract Background Ecological evaluations of mammography screening are confounded by birth-cohort effects and concurrent advances in treatment. We examined the age-period-cohort (APC) structure of breast cancer mortality in Japan and quantified how much screening exposure varies independently of that structure. Methods Deaths among Japanese women aged 30–84 years in 1960–2024 were tabulated by 5-year age group and period and analysed with Holford’s identifiable APC model and quasi-Poisson errors. Screening eligibility (≥ 50 years from 2000; ≥40 years from 2004) was added as an age × period interaction, as binary or cumulative eligibility with lags of 0, 5 and 10 years. Separability was quantified as the R² of exposure on the APC terms. Incidence for 1976–2020 was analysed on the same grid. Results Among 437,134 deaths, the age-cohort model fitted far better than the age-period model (deviance 389.2 vs 9,041.8). The cohort deviation from the log-linear trend peaked in women born around 1950 (rate ratio [RR] 1.51; 95% CI, 1.47–1.54). Incidence, including three high-quality regional registries, shared this peak less markedly than mortality (RR 1.22 vs 1.43, 1976–2020). APC terms explained 91% to > 99% of the variation in screening exposure. With a 10-year lag, eligibility was not associated with mortality (RR 1.005; 0.971–1.040); across definitions, RRs ranged from 0.955 to 1.196. Conclusions Non-linear changes in breast cancer mortality in Japan were aligned mainly with birth cohort. Less than 10% of the variation in screening exposure was independent of the APC structure, so its effect cannot be reliably estimated from national statistics; individual-level linked data are needed.

title: Fatal Holospinal Epidural Abscess: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Holospinal epidural abscess (HEA) is a rare and potentially life-threatening form of spinal epidural infection characterized by extensive involvement of the spinal canal. Its management is particularly challenging because of rapid neurological deterioration, widespread spinal cord compression, and the complexity of surgical intervention. Case Presentation A 56-year-old woman with diabetes mellitus developed rapidly progressive tetraparesis following interventional ozone therapy for severe back pain. Contrast-enhanced spinal magnetic resonance imaging revealed a continuous ventral epidural abscess extending from the clivus to the sacrum, causing extensive spinal cord compression. Imaging also demonstrated suspected L4–L5 vertebral infection and a left psoas abscess. Surgical drainage was performed, and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) was isolated from intraoperative specimens. Despite surgical intervention and broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy, the patient showed no neurological recovery and died 10 days later following clinical deterioration and sepsis. Conclusion This case highlights the exceptional rarity of HEA extending from the clivus to the sacrum, involving nearly the entire spinal canal. Even initially small or localized spinal epidural abscesses may spread extensively along the spinal canal, potentially leading to devastating neurological consequences. Such extensive craniospinal involvement poses significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Therefore, clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for widespread spinal infection in patients presenting with progressive neurological deficits, particularly following spinal interventions. Early recognition, prompt evaluation of the extent of infection, and timely multidisciplinary management are essential to improve clinical outcomes.

title: Multimodal Fusion of Radiomics, Two-Dimensional Deep Learning, and Clinical Risk Factors for Preoperative Prediction of Pathological Complete Response to Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy in Breast Cancer: A Multicenter External Validation Study
abstract: Abstract Purpose Accurate preoperative prediction of pathological complete response (pCR) following neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) is essential for individualized treatment decision-making in patients with breast cancer. This study aimed to develop a multimodal fusion model integrating conventional radiomics, two-dimensional (2D) deep learning features, and clinical risk factors based on the pre-treatment third-phase images of dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI), and to validate its efficacy for predicting pCR in an independent institutional cohort. Methods This retrospective multicenter study enrolled 372 women with breast cancer who received NAC across two centers. The 245 patients from Center 1 constituted the model development cohort and were stratified by pCR status and randomly split at a 7:3 ratio into a training set (n = 171) and an internal validation set (n = 74), whereas the 127 patients from Center 2 served as an independent external test set. A radiologist manually delineated the tumor region of interest on the third contrast-enhanced phase of DCE-MRI, and all delineations were reviewed by a senior radiologist. A total of 1,197 radiomic features were extracted using PyRadiomics; after Spearman correlation-based redundancy removal and dimensionality reduction with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, 10 features were retained to construct the radiomics model. Six ImageNet-pretrained convolutional neural networks were compared, and MobileNet V2 was selected to build the 2D deep learning model. After dimensionality reduction by principal component analysis, the deep features were early-fused with the radiomic features to develop a deep learning radiomics (DLR) model. Independent clinical predictors of pCR were identified using univariate and multivariate logistic regression and used to construct a clinical model. The predicted probability of the DLR model was further fused with the independent clinical factors using logistic regression to build the combined model, which was presented as a nomogram. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, calibration curves, decision curve analysis, the DeLong test, the integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), and the net reclassification improvement (NRI). Interpretability analyses were conducted using SHAP and Grad-CAM. Results The pCR rate of the entire cohort was 14.2% (53/372), with rates of 17.0%, 21.6%, and 6.3% in the training, internal validation, and external test sets, respectively. Multivariate logistic regression identified ER status (adjusted OR = 0.119, P < 0.001), HER-2 status (adjusted OR = 4.870, P = 0.003), and maximum tumor diameter (adjusted OR = 0.742, P = 0.041) as independent predictors of pCR. In the independent external test set, the combined model achieved the best overall discriminative performance, with an AUC of 0.933 (95% CI: 0.879–0.987), accuracy of 0.843, sensitivity of 1.000, specificity of 0.832, and negative predictive value of 1.000, outperforming the clinical model (AUC = 0.925), the deep learning model (0.825), the DLR model (0.745), and the radiomics model (0.559); its AUC was significantly higher than those of the radiomics model (P = 0.0007) and the DLR model (P = 0.014). The deep learning model showed the smallest cross-center performance degradation (ΔAUC = 0.033), markedly smaller than that of the conventional radiomics model (ΔAUC = 0.278). Relative to the four single-modality models, the combined model yielded positive IDI (0.208–0.482, all P < 0.05) and NRI (0.216–0.683) values, good calibration (Hosmer–Lemeshow test, P = 0.069), and a higher net clinical benefit on decision curve analysis. SHAP and Grad-CAM analyses consistently demonstrated that model decisions focused on intratumoral enhancement heterogeneity and peritumoral regions, with the most contributory features derived from both radiomics and deep learning, indicating complementarity between the two sources of information. Conclusions The multimodal fusion nomogram integrating independent clinical predictors, conventional radiomic features, and 2D deep learning features can accurately and robustly predict pCR after NAC in breast cancer before surgery, with favorable cross-center generalizability and interpretability. It may serve as a noninvasive quantitative tool for evaluating NAC response and supporting individualized treatment decision-making.

title: White-Eye Presentation of Endogenous Klebsiella pneumoniae Endophthalmitis with a Choroidal Abscess Secondary to Colorectal Sepsis: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Purpose: Endogenous endophthalmitis is sight-threatening and commonly produces marked ocular inflammation. Klebsiella pneumoniae endogenous endophthalmitis is classically associated with pyogenic liver abscess, whereas colorectal sources and externally quiet presentations are rarely reported. We describe culture-positive multidrug-resistant K. pneumoniae endogenous endophthalmitis with a clinically diagnosed choroidal abscess secondary to colorectal sepsis. Method: Brief report. Results: A 58-year-old man with stage IV rectal adenocarcinoma, tumour perforation and a K. pneumoniae -positive retroperitoneal abscess presented with painless visual deterioration in the left eye. Visual acuity was 6/9 in the right eye and hand movements in the left. Examination of the right eye was otherwise normal. The left eye appeared externally white, without conjunctival injection or lid swelling, despite hypopyon, fibrin and dense vitritis. B-scan ultrasonography showed vitreous loculations, an 11.07-mm dome-shaped choroidal elevation and exudative retinal detachment. K. pneumoniae was isolated from the retroperitoneal abscess, blood and vitreous, supporting haematogenous dissemination. He received four intravitreal injections of vancomycin and ceftazidime with intravenous ceftriaxone. Repeat ultrasonography after two weeks showed persistent vitreous loculations but resolution of the choroidal elevation and a flat retina. Vision deteriorated to no perception of light, systemic instability precluded vitrectomy, and the patient died approximately five weeks later. Conclusion: An externally quiet white eye can conceal severe K. pneumoniae endogenous endophthalmitis. Acute visual deterioration in a septic or immunocompromised patient warrants urgent posterior-segment assessment, vitreous sampling, intravitreal antimicrobial therapy and systemic source control. Visual prognosis remains guarded despite prompt ocular and systemic antimicrobial treatment.

title: SegRef3D Lite: A browser-based workflow for artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation and quantitative three-dimensional morphological analysis
abstract: Abstract Segmentation is a major bottleneck in three-dimensional morphological analysis. Although artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation workflows can be used to address this issue, their implementations are constrained by dedicated software environments or local computing resources. To address these challenges, we developed SegRef3D Lite, a browser-based platform that integrates two complementary artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation approaches (namely, SegAnything and SegCT/MRI) within a common human-in-the-loop workflow. SegAnything provides general-purpose, prompt-based segmentation by using Segment Anything Model 2, and SegCT/MRI provides anatomy-specific segmentations of computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging datasets by using TotalSegmentator. Both approaches generate segmentation masks that can be imported into the same browser-based workspace for visual review, manual correction, quantitative volume measurement, three-dimensional visualization, and surface-model export. In this workspace, routine image handling and refinement are performed locally in the browser, whereas artificial intelligence inference is executed through user-initiated Google Colaboratory workflows, thus eliminating the need for a compatible graphics processing unit on a local computer. We applied our platform to serial block-face photographs, volumetric computed tomography, serial light microscopy, serial electron microscopy, and human abdominal computed tomography. Across these diverse imaging modalities and spatial scales, our platform is able to process outputs from different segmentation approaches by using the same downstream workflow for review, refinement, quantitative analysis, and three-dimensional reconstruction. Therefore, SegRef3D Lite provides an accessible framework for integrating complementary artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation strategies with researcher-guided verification and quantitative morphological analysis. Mini-abstract : SegRef3D Lite integrates general-purpose and anatomy-specific artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation with browser-based human refinement, volume measurement, and three-dimensional reconstruction across diverse morphological imaging modalities.

title: Gadopiclenol Maintains Image Quality at a Reduced Gadolinium Dose for Intracranial Vessel and Aneurysm Wall MRI
abstract: Abstract Background Intracranial vessel wall MRI (VW-MRI) relies on gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCAs) to assess cerebrovascular pathologies. Gadopiclenol is a high-relaxivity GBCA that may provide comparable diagnostic performance at half the gadolinium dose of conventional agents. This study compares the contrast enhancement performance of gadopiclenol with standard-dose gadobutrol for intracranial VW-MRI. Methods In this retrospective single-center study, patients with cerebral aneurysms underwent VW-MRI using either gadopiclenol (0.05 mmol/kg) or gadobutrol (0.1 mmol/kg). Qualitative image quality was independently assessed using four-point Likert scales for overall image quality, subjective noise, border delineation, and vessel wall morphology. Quantitative analyses included enhancement percentage (EP), lesion-to-background ratio (LBR), aneurysm-to-noise ratio (ANR), and normalized signal intensity (SI). Group comparisons used Wilcoxon rank-sum tests with Bonferroni correction. Mixed-effects models accounted for repeated measures and scanner variability. Inter-reader agreement was assessed using ICC and weighted Cohen's κ. Results Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups for all 53 patients and no statistically significant differences were observed between gadopiclenol (n = 26) and gadobutrol (n = 27) groups for any qualitative or quantitative metric after Bonferroni correction. A trend toward improved border delineation with gadobutrol (adjusted p = 0.094) and higher LBR with gadopiclenol (adjusted p = 0.073) did not reach statistical significance. Mixed-effects models confirmed no significant contrast-agent effect on EP ( p = 0.71) or normalized SI ( p = 0.34). Inter-reader agreement was excellent for qualitative image assessment (κ = 0.601–0.947) and good to excellent for aneurysm-specific quantitative metrics (ICC = 0.673–0.805), while background-dependent metrics demonstrated lower reproducibility. Conclusions Half-dose gadopiclenol provided image quality and enhancement metrics comparable to standard-dose gadobutrol, supporting its use for intracranial vessel wall MRI while reducing gadolinium exposure.

title: Robotic-Arm Assisted versus Conventional Total Hip Arthroplasty via the Direct Anterior Approach: Acetabular Cup Positioning, Limb-Length Discrepancy, and Offset Restoration
abstract: Abstract Background Robotic-arm assisted total hip arthroplasty (THA) aims to improve the precision of acetabular cup placement and limb-length restoration. Whether these radiographic advantages translate into clinically meaningful benefits over conventional THA via the direct anterior approach (DAA) remains incompletely characterized. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 330 consecutive patients who underwent primary unilateral THA via the DAA by a single surgeon-led team between January 2021 and January 2025 at a tertiary referral center. In total, 165 patients received MAKO robotic-assisted THA and 165 underwent conventional THA. Indications included osteonecrosis of the femoral head, developmental dysplasia of the hip, rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, and femoral neck fracture. All postoperative radiographic measurements were performed independently by two attending radiologists using a picture archiving and communication system. Primary outcomes comprised acetabular anteversion and inclination, leg-length discrepancy (LLD), and hip offset parameters. title: Can Preoperative PET/CT SUVmax Predict Aggressive Pathological Features in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer? A Retrospective Cohort Study of STAS, LVI, and VPI
abstract: Abstract Background Spread through air spaces (STAS), lymphovascular invasion (LVI), and visceral pleural invasion (VPI) are adverse prognostic features in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that can only be assessed postoperatively. This study evaluated whether preoperative primary tumor SUVmax on 18F-FDG PET/CT independently predicts these features. Methods In this retrospective cohort of 478 patients undergoing surgical resection for NSCLC, associations between primary tumor SUVmax and STAS, LVI, and VPI were assessed using univariate and multivariable logistic regression, adjusted for tumor size, histologic subtype, and other clinically relevant covariates. Discriminative performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Results STAS, LVI, and VPI were present in 269 (56.3%), 237 (49.6%), and 202 (42.3%) patients, respectively. SUVmax was independently associated with all three outcomes: STAS (adjusted OR = 1.051, 95% CI 1.020–1.083, p = 0.001), LVI (adjusted OR = 1.083, 95% CI 1.048–1.119, p < 0.001), and VPI (adjusted OR = 1.044, 95% CI 1.015–1.073, p = 0.002). Discriminative performance was acceptable for LVI (AUC = 0.701) but weak for STAS (AUC = 0.578) and VPI (AUC = 0.584). Sensitivity analyses excluding neoadjuvant-treated patients and interaction testing confirmed these associations were independent of neoadjuvant treatment status. Conclusion Preoperative SUVmax is independently associated with STAS, LVI, and VPI in resected NSCLC, most strongly for LVI. Although its standalone discriminative value is limited, SUVmax—already available at diagnosis—may contribute to multivariable preoperative risk stratification alongside histologic subtype and tumor size.

title: Quantitative Grading of Disc Health and Degeneration from Routine MRI: AI-Based Prediction of T2 Relaxometry Values using Radiomics and a proposal for New Grading
abstract: Abstract Purpose Identifying Disc degeneration (DD) before it is obvious on routine Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is the focus of spine research. Quantitative T2 relaxometry of the nucleus pulposus (T2r) offers objective biochemical evaluation of DD but has disadvantages of high costs, long scan times, and limited availability. We evaluated whether radiomic features derived from standard sagittal T2-weighted(T2W) MRI could accurately predict degeneration status and estimate continuous T2r values, thereby making T2r values available from normal T2W images. Methods We analyzed 621 lumbar intervertebral discs from 160 individuals. A data-derived T2r degeneration threshold was established using a reference cohort of 334 volunteer discs. Discs were partitioned at the patient level into training (353), validation (154), and external validation test set (114 discs). 111 radiomic features were extracted using 3D Slicer. A quantile-transformed logistic regression model was trained to predict binary degeneration (T2r ≤ 82.2 ms), while a Support Vector Regression (SVR) model estimated continuous T2r values. Results The binary radiomics model demonstrated good prediction with an AUC of 0.928 (95% CI: 0.87–0.98) and accuracy of 86.0% on the held-out test set. Importantly, the model correctly identified 70.8% of biochemically altered discs within Pfirmann I and II discs. For continuous modelling, SVR achieved a strong Spearman correlation (ρ = 0.79) with actual T2r values, yielding a low median absolute deviation of 12.2 ms. Conclusion T2r radiomics provides a promising surrogate for advanced quantitative mapping and provides universal access to biochemical disc profiling without need for specialised software, increased time, and costs.

title: Navigated Robotic Guidance for Minimally Invasive Bertolotti Resection: Technical Feasibility and Workflow Evaluation
abstract: Abstract Bertolotti syndrome is characterized by symptomatic lumbosacral transitional vertebral anatomy in which an enlarged transverse process articulates or fuses with the sacrum or ilium. Diagnosis can be difficult because transitional anatomy is common, symptoms may overlap with other spinal disorders, and the pain generator may arise from the pseudoarticulation, adjacent disc or facet, instability, or nerve compression. When targeted nonoperative treatment fails, surgical options include resection, nerve decompression, or fusion depending on anatomy and the dominant pain mechanism. Published evidence supports image guidance for localization and confirmation of resection and describes early robotic assistance for trajectory and incision planning; however, evidence specific to robotic Bertolotti resection remains limited. This article evaluates the feasibility of a preoperatively planned, navigated robotic workflow for minimally invasive Bertolotti resection. A framework is presented for preoperative computed-tomography planning, convergent access through a minimally invasive incision, trajectory-controlled drilling of bone-cut trajectories across the transverse processes and pseudoarticulations, navigated osteotomy, fragment removal and verification of complete decompression or resection. Feasibility was assessed by completion of planned robotic and navigated steps, intraoperative confirmation of registration and resection, and review of technical, perioperative, and imaging outcomes. These concepts may improve reproducibility and reduce challenges related to limited visualization and complex three-dimensional anatomy, but do not prove superior outcomes. This paper outlines a novel technique; however, further comparative studies using standardized measures of pain, disability, operative time, blood loss, radiation exposure, navigation accuracy, resection quality, and reoperation rate are needed before the clinical value of robotic guidance is established.

title: X-ray tomography and coordinate metrology benchmark for internal cavities in additively manufactured alloys
abstract: Abstract X-ray computed tomography (CT) is widely used for dimensional inspection of inaccessible internal geometry, but multi-modal public benchmark datasets with reference metrology remain scarce, particularly for internal cavities. This paper releases a CT--coordinate measuring machine (CMM) benchmark for wall-thickness measurements using CT surface extraction of an artefact with a complex internal cavity that is disassembled for tactile probing. Four cases span Ti-6Al-4V and Inconel 625 in rough and chemically milled states. Each case includes nominal computer-aided design (CAD) geometry aligned to the CT reconstruction, CT projections, reconstructed volumes, CT surface segmentations, CMM point clouds with predefined thickness-pair vectors, and derived surface- and thickness-deviation labels. The paper defines the benchmark tasks and reporting convention and reports baseline results for reconstruction-based and CAD-informed routes. The benchmark permits validation of CT-based dimensional metrology in noisy and clean environments, including CAD-constrained surface reconstruction approaches that work entirely in projection space, such as elastic registration.

title: Technical Success Is Not Clinical Success: Endoscopic Detorsion and Subsequent Clinical Course in a Consecutive Cohort of Sigmoid Volvulus
abstract: Abstract Background Endoscopic detorsion is the initial treatment for uncomplicated sigmoid volvulus, but technical success does not guarantee recovery without further intervention, and procedural outcomes and the later clinical course are rarely reported together. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 46 consecutive adults with sigmoid or rectosigmoid volvulus admitted to one tertiary centre between June 2018 and June 2026. Endoscopic outcome was classified as complete detorsion, decompression without complete detorsion, or failure. Index-admission surgery, documented recurrence and mortality were recorded for each class. Admission variables were examined in exploratory analyses. Results Endoscopy was attempted in 38 patients (82.6%). Complete detorsion was achieved in 22/38 (57.9%; 95% confidence interval 42.2–72.1), decompression without complete detorsion in 3/38 (7.9%) and failure in 13/38 (34.2%). Emergency surgery during the index admission was required in 12 of 13 patients after failure and in 5 of 22 after complete detorsion. No rectal decompression tube was recorded after any complete detorsion. Recurrence was documented in 5 of 12 patients discharged alive after complete detorsion without surgery. Thirty-day mortality was 8/45 (17.8%). One perforation found after a failed attempt could not be attributed with certainty. Lower lymphocyte count and prognostic nutritional index were associated with non-complete detorsion; the composite index showed no demonstrable advantage over lymphocyte count alone. Conclusions Emergency surgery was required during the same admission after 22.7% of technically successful detorsions. Reports of endoscopic treatment should distinguish procedural success from subsequent surgery, recurrence and mortality. The admission-marker associations are exploratory and do not justify a change in treatment selection.

title: Effect of Natural Standing and Rest on Solute Transport Pathways in Hypermobile and Immobile Human Lumbar Intervertebral Discs. Results from Delayed Post-Contrast Upright MRI Study
abstract: Abstract Purpose To examine how physiological states of resting and standing effect the nutrient transport in mobile, hypermobile and immobile lumbar intervertebral discs. Methods This prospective study included 15 healthy participants (10 males, 5 females; mean age, 25.2 ± 3.6 years), divided into three groups: normally mobile, hypermobile (bilateral L5 pars defects), and immobile (lumbosacral transitional vertebrae), with five participants per group. Six-hour delayed post-contrast (0.3mmol/kg) T1-weighted MR images were obtained using a 0.25-T upright positional MRI system in supine, standing, and immediate post-standing recovery positions. Three-dimensional segmentation using 3D Slicer enabled regional enhancement analysis of the central nucleus pulposus (CNP), peripheral nucleus pulposus (PNP), and superior and inferior endplate zones. Results Normal discs showed standing-associated enhancement loss (wash-out) in both CNP and PNP, followed by recovery, particularly peripherally. Hypermobile discs demonstrated the largest standing-associated reduction in CNP enhancement of approximately 2.8 times that of normal discs, with incomplete regain in recovery position. Immobile discs demonstrated the greatest peripheral enhancement loss and limited central recovery. Their superior endplate exhibited a marked, reversible enhancement increase during standing, while the inferior endplate showed comparatively little positional variation. Conclusions For the first time, present study documented acute effects of natural standing and rest on solute transport of human lumbar discs with different mobility patterns in vivo. Despite similar morphology, discs at hypermobile and immobile segments demonstrated different patterns of enhancement wash-out on standing as well as different recovery patterns during rest.

title: PG-HSAM: Prototype-Guided Hierarchical Segment Anything Model for Medical Image Segmentation with Limited Annotations
abstract: Abstract Adapting segmentation foundation models to medical images with limited annotations requires effective use of semantic information without substantially increasing model complexity. We propose PG-HSAM, an extension of H-SAM that introduces prototype prior fusion (PPF) and balanced pixel-to-prototype contrastive regularization (BPC). PPF maintains exponential-moving-average class prototypes, converts pixel-to-prototype similarities into a semantic probability prior, and fuses this prior with the first-stage prediction before hierarchical refinement. BPC regularizes the same feature space with class-balanced pixel sampling. For binary segmentation, foreground and background prototypes are jointly normalized to construct the semantic prior. The prototype memory is non-trainable, and BPC is used only during training. Under the limited-label protocols of H-SAM, PG-HSAM achieves mean Dice scores of 80.49%, 85.20%, and 83.51% on Synapse, LA, and PROMISE12, respectively. Compared with H-SAM, the gains are 0.81, 1.26, and 6.56 percentage points, while Synapse HD95 decreases from 18.35 to 13.70. Ablation and hyperparameter studies further verify the contributions of PPF and BPC and show that the improvement is obtained without increasing the model parameter count.

title: Incremental Value of Pretreatment 18F-FAPI PET/CT and MRI for Predicting Early Treatment Response and Long-Term Prognosis in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Undergoing Chemoradiotherapy​
abstract: Abstract Objectives Effective noninvasive tools for predicting treatment response and prognosis in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) remain lacking. This study aimed to investigate the predictive value of integrating pretreatment 18 F-fibroblast activation protein inhibitor positron emission tomography/computed tomography ( 18 F-FAPI PET/CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for short-term complete response (CR) and progression-free survival (PFS) in patients with NPC undergoing chemoradiotherapy. Materials and Methods This retrospective study analyzed pretreatment 18 F-FAPI PET/CT and contrast-enhanced MRI (CE-MRI) parameters in 46 patients with NPC who underwent chemoradiotherapy. Logistic regression identified predictors of CR and developed predictive models, which were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, DeLong test, bootstrap internal validation, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Cox regression identified independent predictors of PFS, while Kaplan–Meier analysis and log-rank test evaluated survival outcomes. Results Nineteen patients (41.3%) achieved CR, whereas 27 (58.7%) did not. Total lesion fibroblast activation protein expression (TLF), signal intensity ratio (SIR), and radiologic extranodal extension (rENE) independently predicted CR. A multimodal model incorporating these variables achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.88, outperforming PET/CT-only (AUC = 0.76) and MRI-only (AUC = 0.79) models numerically. A maximum standardized uptake value of the primary lesion (SUVmax-T) ≥ 17.0 and the presence of rENE independently predicted shorter PFS. The Sankey diagram illustrated that high-risk parameter combinations were associated with non-CR and shorter PFS, while short-term CR was strongly concordant with longer PFS. Conclusion Pretreatment 18 F-FAPI PET/CT and MRI provide complementary information that may improve short-term response assessment and prognostic stratification in NPC.

title: Saccadic network dysfunction underlies eye-movement variability in early Parkinson's disease
abstract: Abstract Parkinson’s disease is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by altered subcortical-cortical connectivity, leading to motor and cognitive deficits. Saccadic eye movement abnormalities are among the earliest and most persistent markers of the disease, serving as sensitive indicators of disrupted oculomotor and cognitive control. While changes in average saccadic behavioral measures are widely reported in Parkinson's disease, intra-individual variability in saccadic performance and the underlying network dysfunction remain poorly understood. Here, we quantified intra-individual saccadic variability in early-stage Parkinson’s disease and identified its functional correlates within the resting-state saccadic network. We analyzed data from the inclusion visit of 91 patients with early-stage Parkinson’s disease and 46 healthy controls from the ICEBERG cohort (monocentric prospective research study) who underwent oculomotor testing and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging. First, at the behavioral level, we assessed intra-individual variability in saccadic performance within each group using the coefficient of variation of reaction time and normalized peak velocity across trials. Second, at the brain level, we assessed group differences in static and dynamic functional connectivity across 39 regions comprising the saccadic network. We examined the relationship between network connectivity and saccadic variability using partial least squares analysis. We also quantified network organization using graph-theory measures of global efficiency and clustering coefficient. Finally, we tested the relevance of intra-individual saccadic variability and network features in distinguishing patients from healthy controls using a multivariate Mahalanobis classifier. Our results showed that, compared to HC, patients had higher intra-individual variability in saccadic behavioral measures of reaction time (p Holm = 0.012) and normalized peak velocity (p Holm = 0.012). Interestingly, patients had (i) reduced static and dynamic connectivity within the saccadic network and (ii) weaker associations between network connectivity and intra-individual saccadic variability of specifically normalized peak velocity. These results were particularly driven by regions within the cognitive saccade network. The classifier that integrated intra-individual saccadic variability and network connectivity achieved 95.62% accuracy in distinguishing patients from healthy controls, with dynamic connectivity contributing more strongly to classification performance than static connectivity. We demonstrate that elevated intra-individual variability of saccades, underpinned by altered functional connectivity within cognitive-oculomotor networks, is a prominent feature of early-stage Parkinson’s disease. Emerging as a promising physiological marker of disease pathophysiology, intra-individual variability offers a powerful new framework to refine early diagnosis and improve the tracking of neurodegeneration before severe clinical milestones are reached.

Saccadic eye movement abnormalities are among the earliest and most persistent markers of the disease, serving as sensitive indicators of disrupted oculomotor and cognitive control. While changes in average saccadic behavioral measures are widely reported in Parkinson's disease, intra-individual variability in saccadic performance and the underlying network dysfunction remain poorly understood. Here, we quantified intra-individual saccadic variability in early-stage Parkinson’s disease and identified its functional correlates within the resting-state saccadic network. We analyzed data from the inclusion visit of 91 patients with early-stage Parkinson’s disease and 46 healthy controls from the ICEBERG cohort (monocentric prospective research study) who underwent oculomotor testing and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging. First, at the behavioral level, we assessed intra-individual variability in saccadic performance within each group using the coefficient of variation of reaction time and normalized peak velocity across trials. Second, at the brain level, we assessed group differences in static and dynamic functional connectivity across 39 regions comprising the saccadic network. title: Epicardial adipose tissue volume and the Naples Prognostic Score add incremental value to EuroSCORE II for predicting MACE after TAVR: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is a common degenerative valvular disease in the elderly, and transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is now its mainstream treatment. Conventional risk scores based on demographic and comorbidity data do not capture local cardiac inflammation or systemic nutritional status, limiting prediction of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) after TAVR. Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) volume and the Naples Prognostic Score (NPS) reflect these dimensions, but their combined incremental value is unknown. We assessed their independent and incremental value for MACE after TAVR, using EuroSCORE II as reference. Methods In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 427 consecutive patients with severe CAVD undergoing TAVR (January 2020 to July 2025) were enrolled. EAT volume was quantified on computed tomography angiography and dichotomized at the cohort median; NPS was derived from routine laboratory indices and categorized as low (0–2) or high (3–4). The endpoint was MACE after TAVR, defined by Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 criteria. Multivariable Cox regression assessed independent prognostic value; nested models were compared by Harrell’s C-index, time-dependent ROC, net reclassification index (NRI), integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) and decision curve analysis. Proportional hazards were assessed. Results During a median follow-up of 24.51 months, 89 patients (20.8%) experienced MACE. After adjustment, both high EAT and high NPS were independent predictors, with average hazard ratios (HRs) of 3.01 (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.80–5.03; P < 0.001) and 1.96 (95% CI 1.27–3.04; P = 0.003). Adding both markers raised the C-index from 0.716 to 0.751 (likelihood-ratio P < 0.001); the 24-month area under the curve was 0.757. Integrated discrimination improvement was 0.068 (95% CI 0.031–0.134; P = 0.011) and net reclassification index was 0.075 (95% CI − 0.081–0.239; P = 0.345). Calibration and sensitivity analyses supported the model; time-varying analysis showed that the effect of high EAT increased over follow-up whereas that of high NPS was confined to the early period. Conclusions Preoperative EAT volume and NPS are independent, complementary predictors of MACE after TAVR. Their combination improves on conventional risk scores and requires only routine preoperative examinations.

title: Stone Volume Outperforms Linear Measurements in Predicting Ureteroscopic Laser Energy, Especially for Complex Stones
abstract: Abstract Current guidelines use linear measurements to quantify stone burden for urolithiasis, but 3D volumetric assessment may offer superior accuracy. This study compared cumulative stone length and volume as predictors of total laser energy expenditure, a surrogate for operative effort, and established volume-based energy tiers. This was a retrospective analysis of 241 ureteroscopic laser lithotripsy cases (6/10–12/31/24); cumulative stone length and volume were measured from preoperative computed tomography (CT) imaging. Log-transformed multivariable regression predicted laser energy (Joules), controlling for stone number, staghorn status, and Hounsfield units (HU). Regression tree analysis identified distinct energy tiers. Volume predicted laser energy near proportionally (β = 0.93), whereas length overestimated it (β = 1.60). Volume's predictive advantage grew with complexity: for > 3 stones, length lost nearly all predictive value (R 2 = 0.02) while volume remained stable (R 2 = 0.30). For stones ≥ 20 mm, volume doubled length's performance (R 2 = 0.50 vs. 0.22; 36% narrower residual IQR). For volumes ≥ 500 mm³, volume tripled length's performance (R 2 = 0.40 vs. 0.12; 31% narrower residual IQR). Predictive performance was equivalent in low-complexity cases. Regression tree modeling established four energy tiers: <1,235 mm 3 with HU < 1,080 (2,477 J); <1,235 mm 3 with HU ≥ 1,080 (4,940 J); 1,235-2,505 mm 3 (9,625 J); and ≥ 2,505 mm 3 (21,940 J). Laser energy expenditure correlates better with stone volume than length, particularly in complex cases (multiple, large, or dense stones). Stone volumes > 1235 mm 3 and density > 1080 HU emerged as clinically important thresholds for greater laser energy requirement.
